page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.12xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is driven by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 320 MB of shared L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector extensions and matrix acceleration, including AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Memory capacity stands at 384 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, establishing an allocation of 8 GB per physical core. For high-throughput local data operations, the instance bundles 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations position the i7ie.12xlarge in the upper tiers for memory throughput, compute processing, and transactional operations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 224.54 GB/s, while write operations achieve 123.45 GB/s. In Geekbench testing, single-core execution reached 2319, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, while multi-core performance reached 20458. Transactional performance demonstrates high efficiency, registering 71.48 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 26466.5. Instruction-level tests also show solid throughput across data compression, Clang software builds, and CPU-driven matrix inference tasks.

The dense pairing of 30 TB high-speed NVMe storage, fast DDR5 memory, and dedicated compute cores yields strong resource density for disk-bound enterprise workloads. While general-purpose or compute-focused instances provide a more direct hardware balance for purely stateless applications, the i7ie.12xlarge offers favorable efficiency where heavy I/O operations and in-memory caches overlap. Tradeoffs center on the reliance on local, non-persistent NVMe disks and the lack of discrete GPU hardware, which caps throughput on larger generative AI models.

This server type is suitable for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, including distributed NoSQL clusters, search indexing engines, real-time analytics, and data warehousing. It also fits well with memory-intensive ETL pipelines, high-throughput caching systems, and high-concurrency static web serving architectures.
